abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models have been shown to exhibit social biases. abstract: Understanding how artworks are created requires reasoning about the iterative decisions, material operations, and contextual influences that shape artistic production. abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are used worldwide, yet disproportionately reflect Western values, limiting their ability to represent diverse value systems. abstract: Repository-level code generation requires implementing target functions while accounting for complex cross-file dependencies and project-specific conventions. abstract: Research on stereotypes in large language models (LLMs) has largely focused on English-speaking contexts, due to the lack of datasets in other languages and the high cost of manual annotation in underrepresented cultures. title: Buffy versus Bella: An archetypometric analysis and comparison
abstract: Fictional stories and characters embody and encode social norms, and their study is a powerful tool through which to understand culture and society. Vampire stories and folklore, in particular, have long both reflected and refracted people's preoccupation with disease, sexuality, death, and immortality. Here, we explore female main characters from two popular vampire franchises of the 21st century: Buffy Summers from the eponymous Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Bella Swan from the Twilight series.

abstract: Claims about the universality of human concepts have been predominantly assessed through linguistic similarity across languages and cultures. abstract: Composition in Traditional Chinese Paintings (TCPs) carries spatial, narrative, and cultural-aesthetic meaning. Systematic compositional analysis is therefore important for understanding their visual language and artistic meaning. abstract: The paper establishes extra invariant in magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) of rotating and stratified fluid layer. This invariant is conserved adiabatically, i.e. approximately over long time. abstract: The Born rule for computing probabilities of the outcomes of measurements is an indispensable ingredient of quantum mechanics. abstract: Estimating the region of attraction (RoA) of nonlinear systems is fundamental for assessing closed-loop stability and ensuring safe operation. abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) makes inroads into different parts of the Indian subcontinent, there is significant interest in studying how AI impacts the linguistic and cultural foundations of this civilization. abstract: Robustness to domain shift is a key requirement for floor plan generative models to be applicable beyond the single dataset they were trained on, as floor plans vary widely across regions due to distinct architectural cultures, spatial constraints, and construction practices, while acquiring new annotated datasets remains costly and domain-specific. abstract: Audio Descriptions (ADs) narrate visual content for Blind and Low Vision (BLV) audiences during gaps in audiovisual media. abstract: Open web-scale pre-training corpora remain concentrated in English, limiting multilingual LLM development. abstract: Multilingual fluency often invites a stronger assumption: a model that can speak a user's language must also understand the culture encoded by that language. abstract: Restoring incomplete or damaged 3D objects is crucial for cultural heritage preservation, occluded object reconstruction, and artistic design. Existing methods primarily focus on geometric completion, often neglecting texture restoration and struggling with relatively complex and diverse objects. abstract: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of bird diversity across Sri Lanka by integrating spatial, temporal, and environmental data. abstract: This study proposes a novel deep learning framework for automatic detection and classification of mural deterioration patterns in cave temples. Using high-resolution multispectral images of the Mogao Grottoes, we trained a customized ResNet-152 architecture to identify six types of deterioration including flaking, cracking, salt efflorescence, and pigment fading, achieving an overall F1-score of 0.93. The system can process one square meter of mural surface in approximately 3 seconds, making it suitable for large-scale heritage monitoring applications.

abstract: We present a comprehensive knowledge graph for Chinese Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH-KG), integrating data from UNESCO lists, China's national ICH inventory, and local gazetteers. We demonstrate its application in ICH discovery, cross-category linkage analysis, and personalized heritage tourism recommendation systems.

title: 从「申遗热」到「后申遗时代」：中国世界遗产管理的制度变迁与挑战
abstract: 本文系统梳理了中国自1985年加入《世界遗产公约》以来40年的遗产管理历程，将其划分为「申遗驱动期」（1985-2004）、「快速增长期」（2005-2019）和「后申遗时代」（2020至今）三个阶段。文章分析了各阶段的制度特征、主要矛盾和典型案例，提出后申遗时代的核心挑战包括：监测体系薄弱、过度旅游化、社区权益保障不足等，并给出政策建议。

abstract: This paper introduces a combined approach using multi-spectral imaging (MSI) and transformer-based machine learning for the decipherment of ancient Chinese bronze inscriptions. abstract: This study assesses climate change risks for 44 UNESCO World Heritage sites across Southeast Asia using CMIP6 climate projections under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Key findings include: 62% of coastal heritage sites face high flood risk by 2050, traditional masonry structures show increased weathering rates due to temperature-humidity coupling, and 15 sites may require emergency adaptation measures within the next decade.
